reviews.text: I had enjoyed the demo, but my worst fears for the early access release have been realized. The antagonistic design tendencies that were implied by the loss of currency between games have blossomed. The amount of upgrades that have had their benefits nerfed and/or negatives added is completely out of hand. Leveling up and buying upgrades should not feel anticlimactic, even punitive.The core gameplay loop is theoretically still fun, but it's buried beneath too many irritants. Considering refunding.

Buy on sale. The meta progression is very weak, I am a few hours in and my runs have not gotten any longer than my first one. In fact my runs have actually gotten shorter because the way the game is designed it is better to do multiple short runs over risking a longer run and losing all your loot. Also you only get like 2% crit upgrade from each meta upgrade, or 5% hp.. You do not feel this at all. I guess on paper I am like a total of "50% stronger" but again that makes no difference when the game forces me to quit before it gets hard. I do not enjoy this aspect of the game design. I want to go till I die. Also there is no dash system, leaving the game to just be a wasd fest and nothing more. 6/10

Updated Review 9/30/25: I still want to recommend this game but I can't. If the game had launched in this state, it would have been a good spot to grow from a lot of issues, particularly around balance, should have been ironed out by now. Original Review: I would like to recommend this game but it's the grind; it's to damn high. The progression feels extremely poor with the minuscule upgrades you get along the way. They need to figure out something to do with the commander because your AI teammates are brain dead and get stuck on terrain and objectives which leaves you just walking around. If you are the commander you need to be able to command your squad to point in a direction you want to go, not just run around the field shooting at whatever they want. The advertisement video makes it seem like you have abilities (which you do!) but they are randomly dropped, short lived and you don't get to exercise control on when to use them. Also, the music loops too quickly and is fatiguing after the first time you play. Overall, I would give it a bit of time to stew before a purchase (or wait for a sale).

[h3]OUTLOOK:[/h3] [table] [tr] [td] [h3][strike]TRAINWRECK | SUBPAR | ON THE FENCE[/strike] | [b]PROMISING[/b] | [strike]IMPRESSIVE[/strike] [/h3] [/td] [/tr] [/table] [h3]SYNOPSIS:[/h3] [table] [tr] [th][b]IMPRESSIONS:[/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [td] Survivor Mercs is a veritable gem in the making. Its cheerful Cannon Fodder aesthetic is a perfect foil for the A-Team military style setting. Indirect commander movement with the squad in tow, to capture objectives may look casual, but the masses of enemy forces waiting to stop them say otherwise. Meta-progression is already quite substantial and battlefield levelling options give flexibility in preferred playstyles. However, the first few hours can be very grindy until enough upgrades are unlocked. SM is a [b]PROMISING[/b] action roguelite that should be scouted, to determine the right time to parachute into its crazy fun gameplay. [/td] [/tr] [/table] [table] [tr] [td][b]STATUS:[/b][/td] [td]Firmly a Work-in-Progress, though already great fun to play and shows all the desired potential one would hope for in an EA title [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]APPEAL:[/b][/td] [td] Sure to appeal to anyone who likes the idea of a military-themed survivor-lite with an aesthetic reminiscent of Cannon Fodder [/td] [/tr] [/table] [quote=]Key provided by the developer through curator [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32732116-IndieGems/][b]INDIE GEMS[/b] [/url] | Click to follow and receive updates for reviews of a similar nature[/quote] [i]More info below....[/i] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3141709654 [h3]POSITIVES:[/h3] ► AUDIOVISUALS - Cute pixel graphics are remindful of Cannon Fodder. Each op gets its own tracks and while the 2nd one is good, the other x2 are fabulous. Both really adding to the ambience and experience. ► BASE FACILITIES - 14x upgradeable slots at the base deliver a wealth of meta-progression from creating distinct commanders, unlocking soldiers, upgrading cmdr & soldier stats, activating selection rerolls/exclusion when levelling up on the battlefield. ► COMMANDERS - A forgiving design given the ability to create/clone unlimited leaders. Progress is never reset if the current commander dies. They can also be revived at the base or on the battlefield with resources or upgrades. ► CONTROLS - Perfectly playable with either kb/m or controller. Only lacks button prompts for the controller while navigating through the base. ► GAMEPLAY - Already is crazy-fun with the non-confrontation guiding of the commander to objectives and having the squad of soldiers follow, till extraction or the final boss is defeated. It may appear casual in nature but with progress battlefields eventually get claustrophobic. Only the last operation has anywhere near bullet-hell. ► GEAR UPGRADES - 23x varyingly useful commander upgrades provide a good range of in-game options to tailor playstyle from mission to mission. ► SOLDIERS - Already has a strong and varied roster of 15x recruits to unlock, of which 5x can be chosen in mission. Different attack styles and abilities give vital cohesion when moving through hordes of mobs. Classes include: sniper, gunners, grenades, melee, shock, flamer, turrets, healer and explosives. ► STABILITY - No problems with crashes or otherwise. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3141712865 [h3]NEUTRAL:[/h3] ► ACCESSIBILITY - Simple enough, but could do with a few more info screens to explain some of the game's concepts. ► BALANCE - Can be affected on the battlefield by the squad make-up and their upgrades. Though acquiring hordes of currency and resources is curtailed by base limits. Commanders are built with good and bad traits. Some soldier abilities on levelling have negative affects to balance the positives. ► DIFFICULTY - Operations start easy enough and ramp up in challenge with progress. Standard mobs get tougher and more numerous with the introduction of x2 mini-bosses and the final boss. The 2nd op was beatable on first try with a similar squad that defeated the 1st area. The 3rd op looks to be over-stuffed with enemies, likely as it is the final area of content atm. ► ECONOMY SYSTEM - Its 2-tier system gives the impetus to capture and extract resources from the battlefield to expand the base, construct and upgrade facilities, and to unlock soldier and commander upgrades. Around x12 resources also be traded for when required. ► ENEMIES - Standard mobs are varied across all x3 ops but are deja vu when constantly replaying the same op over and over. Wish more variation could be introduced a little more from run to run. ► LONGEVITY - Hard to tell as not all content is in, but x7 ops look too lite. There is no sign of an endless mode, though in theory it should be possible to play the game infinitely once all elements of meta-progression have been achieved. ► OPTIMISATION - Slows down during the latter stages of the last x2 ops when the screen is crawling with enemies. At least with my paltry specs. ► PACING - Initially its very grindy due to the need to farm resources and currency, buff the base, unlock soldiers, and commander and solider abilities. Once enough or the right sort are available, the game gets easier. ► REPLAY VALUE - Already possesses numerous factors that add a little dynamism, but a lot of it is down to the need for farming. Alternate bosses and starting with harder mobs on replaying ops would add some more. ► SCALING - Determined mostly by the players choices and priorities regarding base upgrades over unlocking soldiers or cmdr and soldier upgrades. So this will vary. So far the first two operations can be conquered in a few hours. The 3rd and last operation is over-stacked with many more and harder mobs earlier on. ► STEAM INTEGRATION - Organic achievements. Screen capture. Deck integration. Unknown controller support. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3141722537 [h3]NEGATIVES:[/h3] ► CONTENT - A good deal of content is currently still to be added. There are only x3 playable operations (of the x7 indicated) and understandably the last one seems to be overly set-up to fail/grind. Mechanics look mostly in, especially combat ones. Additional soldiers are likely to be introduced. Though more operations or a mode to generate semi-random ones would be welcome. ► CURTAILED SURPLUS - Resources and currency can be lost if the vault base facility isn't big enough to hold the amount currently held. Otherwise it must be spent to bring it below the level it can be stored. ► POLISH - The GUI has placeholders where more features will be implemented. I envisage more changes to the current version as more content is put in. Minor text issues and some QoL need attention. [h3]SPECIFIC SHORTCOMINGS:[/h3] ► Other players have experienced crashes. ► Special force mini-boss Sidewinder not balanced. Though not a terrible thing. Needs a stronger squad. ► Incorrect resource text in the storage room screen. ► No gear or soldier level indications in the GUI. ► Soldier skill trees are devoid of graphical icons to depict specific upgrades. May be intentional. ► Economy model isn't quite complete. Some resources are not available for purchase or are very rarely found on the battlefield. Other issues have been reported on the forum. Some have been reportedly fixed. At the moment, I don't see anything that's very interesting besides leveling up your Mercs. The different Commanders are just so lame and take more effort than they're worth. Why would I want to RNG different commanders when I don't fully understand the benefits and they all seem so minor. The visuals are great up until the game starts to ♥♥♥♥ itself. I won't go into each little thing as I don't have everything unlocked and a new update is supposed to change how a number of things currently work. So I'll wait until after it to update the review. [h3]Commander Traits are just butts[/h3] [Removed until next update] [H3]Yeah, I don't really like the Armor that much[/H3] [Armory] Everything is just a pile of expensive trade offs that I don't know if they're actually worth it. I don't like the idea of this BUT if I get two opposing gear then I might be able to come out ahead. Which might be the intended purpose but when you're starting off on the game, it just seems like buying negatives. This requires knowledge of what they downgrade at each level. There doesn't appear to be a way to see the Max upgrade of X Gear even if I have purchased and used it in battle. Why can't I see the max level of what I've gotten in a run? That way, it forces players to use it in order to know what it gives. (Basically the Additional Details like what can be found in the Barracks) [h3]There are stats and things that make no sense[/h3] -How can I have 117% Crit Chance at base? My Commander does not attack. The only time I can see some sort of attack from the Commander is shunting barrels, Picking up Banana or Landmines power ups. -Why does the Boss area keep launching attacks even after the large text saying "BOSS DEFEATED" is on screen? I had to literally run around off screen to avoid the ground attacks while at 1 hp. -Why does the storage room not tell me what the item is when attempting to select it during purchase screen? -Why do projectiles keep going after hitting the commander?

For now, I suggest waiting to see how this game develops. It doesn't currently measure up to the high standards set by Vampire Survivors, Brotato, and Halls of Torment. Significant improvements are needed, especially in core mechanics: the animations are lackluster, the bomb dashing has potential but falls short, and the UI needs refinement. Despite its flaws, I'm holding onto my copy because of the game's promising vision, which combines a risk-reward extraction element with an XCOM-like metagame. On the positive side, the game runs adequately on the Steam Deck and suits the device well.

[h1]TLDR[/h1] It's alright. Too grindy, gets boring. [h2]Ramblies[/h2] The idea of mercs and the unlocking of them is good but they lack depth coupled with the grindy balancing and capping of player power right before the builds start to feel decent makes this lackluster compared to other games of this genre. The merc trees are super simple and the balancing is bad. There's really one obvious good tree per merc and the rest are bait. Itemization likewise is braindead due to the lack of balance and there's only a handful of things you look out for. Difficulty jumps a ridiculous amount and result in just grinding until you have the proper unlocks then reroll RNG until you hit the right combinations in order to progress. It's less adapting to the situation instead finding the exact combination needed to win. All of this comes together in a lackluster experience devoid of player expression with a grind that feels monotonously hollow in the end.

[h1][b]组建雇佣小队，血战机器军团[/b][/h1] 《Survivor Mercs》是一款火爆的像素风类幸存者游戏，相比于同类作品做了多项改动，玩家将于枪火交加的战场中组建一支战斗小队，不断完成任务行动击溃机械大军。 本作的世界里机械军队正在肆虐，玩家扮演雇佣兵首领开始了这场对抗之旅，游戏打造了多个区域和任务供玩家逐步推进。 游戏引入了超酷的克隆设定，每次出击前都可以选择克隆一个自己的克隆体，克隆体将会从已有的基因库中随机出不同的特性。 每次开始出击都是一次大规模的行动，其由多个任务组成，类型多种多样，诸如获取战利品、坚守一段时间、击败Boss等，这些任务分布在一张类似于《杀戮尖塔》的分支路线上，玩家可按需选择。 随后便可进入类似于《吸血鬼幸存者》的大地图了，系统会不断刷出各种资源点，前往便可获取局内升级用的狗牌、局外解锁用的血钻、新的队友等内容。 游戏的整体节奏较快，每个任务的时间不会很长，完成后队伍等级和升级内容会继承到下一任务，这样一来培养团队的目标很明确，玩家只需要按需升级即可。 玩家控制的角色需要自行开火，队友则会跟随角色一同移动并自动开火，前期队伍等级较低时建议优先增加队友，这样战斗力会迅速上来。 游戏手感和打击感做的不错，角色拥有两段充能式冲刺，冲刺到炸药桶还能将其击飞打击敌人。 《Survivor Mercs》相比于其它类幸存者游戏制作更为精良，除此之外还加入了简单的基地建设玩法，整体来说体验很不错，值得推荐。 [quote]热爱游戏，畅玩游戏，分享游戏，专注鉴赏评测与深度解析 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44110339/]游理游据[/url]，走进游戏世界，品味第九艺术[/quote]

游戏的设计很好，但不合理的地方太多了。 首先是操作问题，主页使用单鼠标很难流畅的浏览，必须配合键盘才行，这样太不方便了。 游戏内属性的加成很迷惑，很难理解加成的具体内容和属性增益，好像每个属性都有影响又好像都没影响，特别是还有负面buff相当难受。也不知道是不是翻译的问题，持续时间增加对绝大多数角色有效，但特别标明对持续伤害无效，到底增加的是什么持续时间？ 难度曲线也相当令人迷惑，前一张图和后一张图难度差别相当大，总体来说游戏前中期都是挺难的，基本享受不到割草的乐趣。 bug影响游戏体验，在多次查看建筑升级之后升级需要材料的UI会消失，还有打boss不造成伤害，退出游戏再进直接从开局图重新来。

Edit, 05/28/26. Not much has changed. Conduit still pops up useless advice boxes, hints you can figure out in the first minutes of the game, all she does is distract you from watching out for ever increasingly annoying enemies... (And yes, achievements have been fixed, and the game is more balanced now, but some mobs like drones thrown at you at the start must be a bad joke.) 5+/10. --- Awe-inspiring visuals, nicely intimidating mood, lots of weaps and chars... and horribly balanced. The grind starts right at the 2nd stage and forces you to repeat runs just to level up stats to not be one shot by anything. What the hell?... Plus, Conduit distracting and offering useless hints, losing all the loot to block progression is just wow. No rare resources dropping is even bigger bs. Achievements broken for months is not exactly a plus either...
